mike-sales: Streamline Health finished perf runs. Need a short customer-facing latency line, a tiny CSV (p50/p95/p99) and a note about failover behavior. cc @tara-eng @jon-sre @ana-se

streamline-rep: Ran three tests: steady 140 r/s, short spike to 500 r/s for 2m, and regional failover (primary -> secondary). Artifacts: https://s3.company/internal/poc/streamline/2178/report.zip

tara-eng: test commands (k6):
```
k6 run --vus 150 --duration 6m script_baseline.js
k6 run --vus 600 --duration 3m script_spike.js
```
// POST /v1/generate max_tokens=256 stream=false

jon-sre: quick numbers (256-token gen):
- baseline (140 r/s): p50=32ms, p95=170ms, p99=380ms
- spike (500 r/s): p50=40ms, p95=510ms, p99=1.5s, errors ~0.8%
- failover: p50=58ms, p95=430ms, p99=980ms (DNS + cross-region hop)

ana-se: Suggested one-liner for SOW: "On dedicated pools sized for your sustained QPS, expect p95 ≈170ms for a 256-token generation (3B-class model). Short bursts above provisioned QPS may increase p99; burst pools or tuned autoscale policies mitigate tail latency."

mike-sales: Good. Add parenthetical about failover bumping p50 due to inter-region hops.

streamline-rep: Confirmed tests used synthetic prompts only; logs scrubbed, no PII.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: nodes 5 -> 10 @ 2178004455 (cooldown=18s)

jon-sre: observations/recs:
- LB queueing starts ~420 r/s; consider burst pool or lower LB queue depth for predictable tails.
- reduce autoscale cooldown to 10s for bursty apps; pre-warm strategy for short spikes.
- for failover, use DNS TTL trickle + client retry to avoid thundering to secondary.

mike-sales: Can someone drop a tiny CSV in the S3 path for the deck? format: scenario,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms

tara-eng: Uploaded /streamline/2178/latency_summary.csv with:
baseline,32,170,380
spike,40,510,1500
failover,58,430,980

mike-sales: Thanks all — will send consolidated deck + SOW tomorrow AM if no objections. :rocket:
